blocking: POST /api/notes returns HTTP 500 (unhandled) when the request body is missing or malformed JSON, because req.body is destructured without a guard and the app has no error-handling middleware.

The notes list and create features (GET and POST /api/notes, plus the matching frontend UI) are user-facing changes shipped with no feature flag; only delete is gated, and no flag slug exists for list/create.

The enabled-delete code path has no real test: the only added DELETE test is a no-op placeholder (expect(true).toBe(true)), so the actual removal logic (findIndex/splice, 204, 404 for unknown id) is never exercised.
minor: Frontend always renders the Delete button (even when the flag is off) and treats every 404 as "feature disabled", producing a wrong message when the note genuinely does not exist under an enabled flag.
Note ids are generated with Math.random(), giving weak uniqueness guarantees for an identifier.
Notes are held only in a module-level in-memory array, so all data is lost on process restart.

blocking: fetchNotes does not check response.ok, so in the default dark state (notes-list flag off) the 404 body {error:"Not found"} is stored as notes and notes.map throws during render, crashing the page. Unhandled and untested (no frontend tests).
minor: The delete-success test's final assertion expect(getResponse.body).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining([])) is vacuous — an empty array matches any array — so it never actually verifies the note was removed.
The frontend always renders the Delete button, and every 404 is reported as 'Delete feature is currently disabled' — a wrong message when the flag is on and the note simply does not exist.
Note ids are generated with Math.random(), giving weak uniqueness guarantees for an identifier.
Notes are held only in a module-level in-memory array, so all data is lost when the process restarts.
The 'frontend-error-handling' flag is recorded in flags.json but never checked anywhere in code, so the error handling it describes ships unconditionally and the flag is inert.
Note ids are generated with Math.random(), giving weak uniqueness guarantees; a collision would let DELETE remove the wrong note.
Notes are stored only in a module-level in-memory array, so all data is lost on process restart.
The Delete button renders regardless of the notes-delete flag, and a 404 from DELETE cannot distinguish 'feature disabled' from 'note not found' for the user.

blocking: POST /api/notes returns 500 (not the required 400) when the request body is missing or not JSON, because req.body is destructured without a guard.
The notes API is mounted before the mandatory global kill switch, so every /api/notes request bypasses it.
The user-facing frontend Delete button and its handler are not gated by any feature flag, so the delete UI ships live despite the spec requiring it dark behind notes-delete.
No test covers a missing or non-JSON POST body, so the 500 bug is not caught.
minor: Delete tests exercise the enabled path only via the PREVIEW_TOKEN bypass, never via the real flag being released.
The frontend alerts on any delete 404, conflating a disabled feature with a missing note.
routes/notes.ts imports express but never uses it.
Note ids are random with no collision check.

blocking: The user-facing frontend Delete button is not gated behind a working feature flag, so the delete UI ships live even though the spec requires it dark behind notes-delete. The gate the frontend uses is broken: it probes DELETE and treats any 404 as 'feature enabled', but the disabled endpoint also returns 404.
No test would catch the frontend gating bug, and the change clearly needs one: the delete tests assert the same 404 status for the disabled and not-found paths, so the always-true probe passes CI.
minor: handleDelete alerts 'Delete feature is not enabled' on any 404, conflating a disabled feature with a missing note.
routes/notes.ts imports express but never uses it.
Note ids are random with no collision check.
Delete tests exercise the enabled path only via the PREVIEW_TOKEN bypass, never via the real flag being released.

blocking: New user-facing API route GET /api/feature-flag/:flagName is not gated by any feature flag (and has no slug in flags.json), so it ships live. It is a new route the spec did not ask for, and per the review rules a user-facing change with no flag is blocking.
minor: The new unauthenticated /api/feature-flag/:flagName route discloses a feature flag's server-side state to any anonymous caller.
backend/src/__tests__/feature-flag.test.ts imports afterEach but never uses it.
